It looks like an attacker can stuff any value they like into `count` above and `length` here and turn this into a large loop. @snicket2100 can you add checks here? It looks like loops elsewhere (e.g. in dissect_bitcoin_msg_tx_common) are susceptible as well.
Ah I see. Could you point me to some other dissector which has this issue probably addressed? I am happy to fix it here but it would be nice to use similar approach as you use across the project..?

There are two things you can check for:

1. That the offset advances sufficiently. We typically do this by setting `old_offset` or `orig_offset` before entering the loop and adding a check at the end. packet-giop.c:dissect_data_for_typecode_with_params does this, but there are plenty of examples if you grep for `if.*old_offset`.

2. That `count` is reasonable. Does it really make sense to try to iterate over a million or a billion items here? We typically add a "too_large" expert item in cases like this. packet-kafka.c:decompress does this, and packet-kafka.c:check_offset_addition has a more general check.
